title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes (third version), Grothendieck is axiomatising a 'tame' or 'multiplicity' structure. The data is a set M of closed 'pieces' (cells, simplices, polyhedra) carrying primitive relations. On this page he changes the choice of primitives to three relations. (i) X ≤ Y: X is a face or closed part of Y. (ii) X ≪ Y: a 'strictly inside' or relative-interior relation. (iii) X |∘| Y: heuristically X° ∥ Y°, i.e. the interiors of X and Y are disjoint. The previous page motivates (iii): it lets one speak of X° even when one cannot decide whether X° is empty. For a simplicial multiplicity the naive definition X° = supp X ∩ cosupp ∂X gives an empty X° except in degenerate cases.

Key definition. Write X̃ = {X' ≤ X}, the closed down-set (the 'closure' of X in the poset). Put L = X̃ ∩ Ỹ; the margin calls this the largest common closed part. Then
 X ≭ Y ⟺ ∀X' ∈ X̃∖L, ∀Y' ∈ Ỹ∖L, X' |∘| Y'.
In modern terms, X and Y are 'compatible' or 'in good position': apart from their common closed subcomplex L, their remaining faces have pairwise disjoint interiors. Hence X ∪ Y is a regular cell complex whose cells are faces of X or of Y. This is exactly the condition that two polytopes meet in a common face (subcomplex). The margin notes that this definition does not use ≪.

Axiom bookkeeping.
- The old axioms Prot Λ1–Λ5 of p.51 are specialised to Λ = M and become Mag 1'', 2'', 3''.
- Mag M1, M3 and M4 are kept.
- M2 becomes tautological when Λ = M.
- M5 will follow from new axioms that replace AtL3.

New axiom Mag 4'': distinct faces Y ≠ Z of a common X satisfy Y |∘| Z. That is, the open cells of a closed cell partition it, as in a regular cell complex.

Lemma (heredity): if X ≭ Y, X' ≤ X and Y' ≤ Y, then X' ≭ Y'.
Notation: L' = X̃' ∩ Ỹ', X'_L = X̃' ∩ Ỹ, Y'_L = Ỹ' ∩ X̃, so L' = X'_L ∩ Y'_L. Take X'' ∈ X̃'∖L' and Y'' ∈ Ỹ'∖L'.
- If neither lies in L, the hypothesis X ≭ Y applies directly.
- If X'' ∈ L, then X'' ∈ Ỹ and also Y'' ∈ Ỹ' ⊂ Ỹ. Moreover X'' ≠ Y'', since equality would put them in L'. So Mag 4'' (applied to Y) gives X'' |∘| Y''.
- The case Y'' ∈ L is symmetric.

Corollary: X ≭ Y and X ≠ Y imply X |∘| Y.
- If X, Y ∉ L, apply the definition directly.
- If X ∈ L, then X < Y and Mag 4'' applies.
A further axiom Mag M6 (ex Prot Λ6) is announced.

Purpose: the next page adds Mag 5''. This says |∘| is symmetric, antireflexive, and stable under shrinking via the ≪∘ relation. Together with this Corollary it yields Mag 5 (existence of a common face containing a given Z ≪ X, Y) and then ∥ characterised via |∘| (Proposition 1). The overall goal is a purely combinatorial or order-theoretic axiomatics of 'tame' polyhedral or semi-analytic space structures, in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' programme.
errors: The proof only treats the case X'' ∈ L and says nothing of the case Y'' ∈ L; that case is symmetric, using Mag 4'' for X.
The proof uses X'' ≠ Y'' without saying why. It follows since X'' = Y'' would lie in X̃'∩Ỹ' = L'. This is fine but implicit.
Otherwise the lemma and corollary are correct given Mag 4''.

ideas.what: Taking 'interiors disjoint' (X |∘| Y) as a primitive relation on a poset of closed cells, so that interiors need never be defined as sets.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic regular cell complexes / face posets with an interior-disjointness relation; point-free approach to tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Face-poset approaches to regular CW complexes: Björner (CW posets, 1984); point-free topology: Johnstone et al.; tame topology: van den Dries (o-minimal structures)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is called for in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6, but not this axiomatics

ideas.what: Definition of 'good position' X ≭ Y: off the largest common closed part L, all faces have pairwise disjoint interiors.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of cells (two cells meet along a common subcomplex), as in the definition of a polyhedral/regular cell complex

ideas.what: Axiom Mag 4'': distinct faces of a cell have disjoint interiors; the lemma that good position is inherited by faces; the corollary that distinct cells in good position have disjoint interiors.
ideas.modern_name: Open cells of a regular CW complex partition it; subcomplex heredity

missed.claim: Grothendieck is building a point-free, order-theoretic axiom system (Mag axioms with primitives ≤, ≪, |∘|) for tame or polyhedral spaces. Interiors and supports are derived rather than primitive, aimed at contexts where one cannot decide whether X° is empty. This axiomatics was never completed or published, and no later literature develops tame topology in exactly this relational-poset form.
missed.quote: Je vais prendre comme relations primitives dans M ≤, ≪, |∘|
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions, with combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path posets), and with constructive/point-free topology. These are the places a decidability-free notion of interior is relevant. The page itself, however, contains only routine lemmas.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine step: a cell-complex compatibility relation and a heredity lemma with a correct short proof. The broader unpublished axiomatic programme is of historical interest, but this page adds nothing a specialist would find surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'Y''=Ỹ'∖L'' in the manuscript should be read as Y'' ∈ Ỹ'∖L'.
The struck-through symbol before 'L=X̃∩Ỹ' in the proof line is a struck ≭, consistent with the transcription's [-≭-].
'version "ensembles spéciaux"' / 'ensembles polyédral': the first word is uncertain and may be 'espaces' or 'complexes'; the image is ambiguous.
